$comment: False-positive budget (task T-10). Contracts that are widely held, heavily
audited, and long-lived. CI asserts each produces zero High or Critical
findings. blockscan passes this gate today; the point of adding it is to
keep passing it after a refactor nobody remembers making.
This is the gate that catches the specific failure the comparison subject
demonstrates: it rates WETH9 critical at 100/100 on five separate false
findings, and none of its 320 tests notices.
SEEDING STATE — READ THIS BEFORE USING THE FILE.
Only entries with verified=true were confirmed against real scan output.
Everything else is specified as a SELECTION PROCEDURE rather than an
address, because an audit corpus containing a wrong address is worse than
no corpus: it produces a green gate that proves nothing. Fill the
candidates in from a block explorer, verify each, and flip verified to
true with the block you pinned it at.

gate.assertion: zero findings of severity High or Critical on every entry
gate.rationale: A warning in CI output is a warning nobody reads. This assertion is the only thing standing between a rule regression and a customer seeing a blue-chip contract rated critical.

entries.name: WETH9
entries.verified_how: present in real scan output examined during this audit; source verified, contract_name WETH9, holding ~2.44M ETH
entries.why_in_set: The single most-held contract on Ethereum and the exact contract the comparison subject mis-rates. If one entry survives a corpus rebuild, it should be this one.

known_acceptable_findings.reason: WETH9 is solc 0.4.x. The finding is correct and below the gate threshold; recorded so a future reader does not mistake it for noise.

candidates_to_seed.$comment: Categories, not addresses. Each is chosen to exercise a different part of the detector surface, so a regression in any one family is caught by at least one entry. Resolve each to a real address, verify it, then move it into entries.

required.criteria: A top-3 stablecoin by supply, deployed behind an upgradeable proxy, source verified.
required.exercises: proxy resolution, implementation fetch, owner-control rules (OWNER_BLACKLIST_CONTROL is expected to fire at Low — verify it stays Low, since a blacklist is intentional in this class and a severity drift would break the gate)

required.criteria: A canonical constant-product AMM pair contract, source verified, high TVL.
required.exercises: ORACLE_SPOT_PRICE_FROM_RESERVES must NOT fire on the pair itself — the pair holds the reserves, it does not read them as a price. This is the highest-value single entry for oracle-rule precision.

required.criteria: The router paired with the AMM above.
required.exercises: MEV_SWAP_DEADLINE_BLOCK_TIMESTAMP and MEV_SWAP_ZERO_AMOUNT_OUT_MIN must not fire on a router that correctly takes deadline and minimum-out as parameters.

required.criteria: A major lending protocol's core market or comptroller, source verified.
required.exercises: Chainlink staleness rules and access-control rules on a contract that does guard correctly.

required.criteria: A widely-forked on-chain governor with a timelock.
required.exercises: The three GOV_ rules must not fire on a governor that does use a timelock and a non-zero proposal threshold.

required.criteria: A large, long-lived NFT collection, source verified.
required.exercises: ERC-721 interface detection, and the reentrancy rule on a contract using safeTransferFrom callbacks legitimately.

required.criteria: A factory deploying EIP-1167 clones, plus two of its clones.
required.exercises: Minimal-proxy detection, clone clustering, and the T-11 shared-implementation rule — this slot is the one that gives the protocol layer a real positive case.

candidates_to_seed.target_size: 10 contracts. Small on purpose: every entry must be individually justified and individually reviewed when it fires. A large known-good set that nobody reads is a rubber stamp.

maintenance.pinned_block_rationale: A known-good contract behind a proxy can be upgraded. Without a pinned block the gate silently changes what it asserts, which is the same defect as task T-04 seen from the corpus side.
on_gate_failure: Do NOT add the rule to the suppression file. Suppression drops findings before scoring and would hide the regression from the metric as well as the gate.
Do NOT lower the entry's expected severity to make it pass.
Either the rule regressed and the rule is fixed, or the finding is genuinely correct and belongs in known_acceptable_findings with a written reason.
maintenance.review_cadence: Re-pin on each release. A stale pin is still reproducible, which is the property that matters; a moving pin is not.
